scenes.title: E minor
scenes.subtitle: Two fingers, six strings.
lines: This lesson teaches the E minor chord — two fingers, six strings.
Play it with confidence as you build your first chords.

scenes.heading: E minor (Em)
points: Curl fingers to avoid string noise
lines: Place finger 2 on string 5, fret 2, and finger 3 on string 4, fret 2.
Curl your fingers so they don't touch other strings.
Strum all six strings — the sound is rich and full.
The E minor chord uses all six strings — let's place your fingers and strum with confidence.
Here's how it sounds: strummed, then string by string.
scenes.tip: Every string belongs to this chord, so strum all six with confidence. Stay on your fingertips so the open G string rings.

scenes.heading: Troubleshooting a chord
lines: Check each string of the Em chord from low to high.
If a string sounds muted or buzzy, adjust your finger—press closer to the fret or arch it slightly.
Small changes make a big difference.
You're doing great—keep experimenting until it feels right.

points: Curl fingers to avoid string noise
